A solution manual tells you the steps. It almost never tells you why anyone
would have tried those steps, which is the only part you actually need to learn.

Every problem here is worked in the same shape:

1. **What is being asked** — restated in plain language, with the physical
   situation described before any symbol appears
2. **What we know** — the givens, the assumptions, and explicitly which
   assumptions are doing real work
3. **Choosing an approach** — the part solution manuals skip. Why energy
   conservation here rather than kinematics, and what would have happened if we
   had guessed wrong
4. **The work** — every algebraic step, none of them called obvious
5. **Sanity check** — units, limiting cases, and whether the number is the right
   size for the physical world

::: {#problems}
:::
